svg.text: Stage A, all 5 servos + OLED on the breadboards (no soldering)
Servo power comes from the kit's Power Supply Module on its own rail, never from the ESP32. The ESP32 runs from the PC's USB. Grounds joined.
Holes a-e of one row are joined; so are f-j. Each rail (+ or -) is one long strip down the board.
plugs in past the end of the boards
sockets face outward, off the board
Jumpers (holes on the RIGHT board unless marked L):
rail bridge: right outer + row 8 -> L outer + row 8
rail bridge: right outer - row 10 -> L outer - row 10
ground join: b29 (ESP32 GND row) -> right outer - rail
signals: e22 D18 -> servo 0, e21 D19 -> servo 1, e16 D23 -> servo 2,
L f21 D32 -> servo 3, L f22 D33 -> servo 4
each servo red -> + rail, brown -> - rail next to it
OLED: GND d29, VCC d30 (3V3), SCL d17 (D22), SDA d20 (D21)
ESP32 in rows 16-30 (EN / D23 in row 16): its USB hangs off the bottom end.
Module on the TOP end of the right board, sockets facing up, off the board.
Its 4 legs per side: 2 in the red + strip, 2 in the blue - strip, rows 4-5.
Every rail pair here: red + strip on the left, blue - strip on the right.
Both jumpers on 5V (5V-VCC pair): both rail pairs of the right board are 5 V.
The inner pair runs under the ESP32: plug nothing of the ESP32 into it. Switch IN.
Meter the rail before plugging servos: ~5 V. 9 V battery: ~700 mA at most.
C1: long leg in the + rail (row 12), striped leg in the - rail (row 13).
Unplug USB and the module's power while wiring. Plug servos one at a time, test each on the Servo control page.
